title: state-averaged exact big-Phi hardens H_345: the basin<->Phi coupling is robust to sys_state choice
question: H_345 measured exact Phi at a SINGLE sys_state=21. Does the basin<->Phi coupling survive averaging exact Phi over ALL 32 sys-states (state-averaged big-Phi)? Or was the single-state coupling an outlier?
engine: pure hexa-lang. n=5 ECA (32 states): basin via 50-step settle + state-AVERAGED EXACT IIT4 phi_structure (stdlib/consciousness/iit4_relation), mean over all 32 sys-states. Pearson over 4 rules {110,30,105,150}. Sharded per-rule (4x32 exact phi_structure exceeds single-run wall budget); Pearson computed from the 4 shard points by a phi_structure-free aggregate.hexa.
runtime: $0 mac-local (abs-path imports resolve here) · deterministic · per-rule parallel shards

falsifier_eval.F346_1_SIGNS_PRESERVED_UNDER_AVERAGING: PASS — state-averaged Pearson(max_basin, mean_Phi) = +0.550 keeps the single-state(21) positive sign (+0.251); Pearson(n_attr, mean_Phi) = -0.951 keeps the single-state negative sign (-0.799). NO sign flip under 32-state averaging. The H_345 single-state coupling is NOT an outlier.
falsifier_eval.F346_2_AVERAGING_TIGHTENS: PASS — both correlations STRENGTHEN under averaging (max_basin +0.251 -> +0.550; n_attr -0.799 -> -0.951). State-averaging removes single-state noise, so the coupling is a cleaner signal, not a fragile one.
falsifier_eval.F346_3_BIJECTION_PHI_IDENTICAL: PASS (consistency) — the two bijection-class rules 105 and 150 have IDENTICAL state-averaged Phi (15.5625 = 15.5625), consistent with H_330's four-moment bijection collapse (105 == 150 == identity-class).

verdict_derived: 🟢 SUPPORTED-NUMERICAL — state-averaged exact big-Phi (mean over all 32 sys-states at n=5) preserves BOTH n=5 single-state signs and tightens them: max_basin<->Phi +0.251 -> +0.550 (positive), n_attr<->Phi -0.799 -> -0.951 (negative). H_345's single sys_state=21 was therefore representative, not an outlier — the basin<->Phi coupling is robust to state choice. This removes H_345's 'single sys_state=21' honest-limit and is the capstone of the self-correction² arc (H_341 n=4 exact -> H_343 n=6 proxy apparent-flip -> H_345 n=5 exact restores signs -> H_346 state-averaging hardens it). The n_attractor_states<->Phi coupling is the dominant, robust cross-family bridge, now -0.95 under averaging: rules whose dynamics concentrate onto few on-cycle states robustly carry higher integration. Bonus consistency: the bijection rules 105/150 carry IDENTICAL state-averaged Phi (15.5625), matching H_330's bijection-class collapse.
structural_vs_dynamical: Cross-family (basin DYNAMICAL x state-averaged-exact-Phi STRUCTURAL), proxy-free, state-marginalized. The decisive finding: H_345's coupling is not an artifact of one chosen initial state; the 32-state marginal preserves and sharpens it. n_attr<->Phi is the robust bridge (-0.80 single-state -> -0.95 state-averaged).
honest_limits: 4 rules / Pearson n=4 still fragile; the max_basin<->Phi correlation, though strengthened to +0.55, is still pulled down from a naive monotone by rule30 (highest Phi 41.36, small basin 6) — the same inversion H_345 flagged
n=5 only for exact state-averaged Phi (n>=6 the full 2^n state sweep is intractable); large-n state-averaging stays open
execution was sharded per-rule for wall-time; each shard is byte-identical reproducible and the run.hexa (full 4-rule) remains the canonical source
state-averaging here is the unweighted mean over all 32 sys-states; a stationary-distribution-weighted average could differ and is not tested
discovery_note: H_345 단일 sys_state=21 결합의 강건성 확정: 32-state 평균 exact Φ로 두 부호 모두 보존+강화 (max_basin↔Φ +0.251→+0.550, n_attr↔Φ -0.799→-0.951). 단일 state는 outlier 아님. self-correction² arc capstone (H_341→343→345→346), H_345 'single-state' honest-limit 제거. bijection rule 105/150 state-avg Φ 동일(15.5625) = H_330 bijection collapse 일관성. n_attr↔Φ가 robust bridge (-0.95).
